newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament opposes efforts to bury Lenin.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament opposes efforts to bury Lenin.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament urged citizens and the authorities on Monday to oppose burying the mummified body of Soviet state founder Vladimir Lenin.

In a non-binding resolution, the State Duma branded attempts to remove the embalmed body from its Red Square mausoleum "an act of political revenge against Lenin" that would ruin the square's historical associations.
A total of 232 deputies backed the resolution and eight were against, though little more than half the 450-strong body took part in the vote.

The fate of Lenin's body has become a subject of heated debate in Russia, especially since President Boris Yeltsin's call for a national referendum on the issue. The president has long supported the removal and burial of the corpse.
His proposed referendum would also decide the fate of dozens of other leading Soviet figures buried by the Kremlin wall.
A recent opinion poll showed that Russians were split roughly 50/50 over burying Lenin.
Yeltsin says it is un-Christian to keep a dead body on display and argues that the Bolshevik leader himself had wanted to be buried.

The communists have aggressively denounced Yeltsin's proposal as "sacrilegious", saying that no one can deny Lenin's role in turning the Soviet Union into a superpower feared by the rest of the world. They say Lenin, who died in 1924, never expressed any wish as to the fate of his body.
The communists warn that any attempt to remove Lenin from Red Square could provoke public unrest across the country.
Russian Orthodox Patriarch Alexiy II last week urged extra caution in deciding whether to remove the body, though he said the people should have the last word.
After the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, Yeltsin removed guards of honour from the mausoleum but it is still open to the public.
